mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) signals inflationary pressures that may lead the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI increases do not correlate with subsequent FEDFUNDS rate hikes.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increases do not correlate with subsequent negative economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strengthening demand in the housing market, which can boost economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of periods following sustained HOUST increases, or HOUST increases do not correlate with subsequent positive economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a contraction in supply-side activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO declines do not correlate with subsequent negative economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening monetary policy, which can stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decreases do not correlate with subsequent positive economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand, which can boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or RSAFS increases do not correlate with subsequent positive economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which can boost consumer confidence and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint increase in PAYEMS and decrease in UNRATE do not correlate with subsequent positive economic indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) signals a strengthening economy, which can boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially during late-cycle expansion.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of periods following sustained GDPC1 increases, or GDPC1 increases do not correlate with subsequent positive economic indicators during late-cycle expansion.
